reference_observations.description: Literal report of eight rather than six permanent incisors is the surviving historical quotation. Whole correspondence, covering question and original date remain unknown; the editorial horse context is not recovered letter prose.

corrections.description: The worker incorrectly converts publication by 1868 into proof of later original correspondence. The original Brown letter is missing and could be earlier; the publication provides an upper bound only. Preserve Brown’s literal quotation within Darwin’s published framing, not a full incoming body.

The surviving printed reply establishes Darwin’s attributed views on lifelong confinement and the breeding argument. It does not automatically endorse every proposal in Rusden’s missing works; some claims occur only in editorial apparatus. Preserve the 1875 context and incomplete extent.

Clowes reports index copy received that morning and a proof planned for tonight before the complaint arrived. This is the firm’s explanation, not independently proven causation of the delay, and not Charles’s voice.
